Class ApiKeysController

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.apikey.ApiKeysController
@RestController public class ApiKeysController extends Object
The caller's API keys under /who/me/api-keys:
  • GET lists them, by name, lastUsedAt null for a key that never signed in;
  • POST with {name, lifetime, scopes} makes one (lifetime an ISO-8601 duration) and answers 201 with the raw key;
  • POST /{id}/rotations with {overlap} (an ISO-8601 duration) replaces one, as ApiKeyService.rotate(UUID, Duration) does, and answers 201 in the same shape;
  • DELETE /{id} revokes one, 204;
  • GET /current answers the key that signed this request in, in the list's shape.

The raw key is in the two 201 bodies (CreatedApiKey) and nowhere else: not in a list, not in /current, not in a log line or an exception.

A browser session (a who session cookie with no API key or bearer token beside it) or a bearer token may manage keys. A browser needs a recent sign-in to make or rotate one; a bearer token does not. A request an API key signed in is 403 ApiKeyCannotManageKeysException everywhere but /current, so a key never mints, lists or revokes keys; a session cookie with an API key or bearer token beside it is 403 BrowserSessionRequiredException; /current without an API key is 404. A signed-out request is 401. A key that does not exist and one that belongs to someone else are both 404, the same answer. A body over 8192 bytes, or a lifetime, overlap, name or scope who refuses, is 400.

      public ApiKeysController(ApiKeyService keys, WhoSessionSecurityContextRepository sessions, tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper jsonMapper, Clock clock, Duration recentSignIn)
      Creates the controller.
      Parameters:
      keys - makes, lists, rotates and revokes the keys
      sessions - reads the browser's who session and its sign-in time
      jsonMapper - reads the request bodies
      clock - the current time
      recentSignIn - how recently a browser session must have signed in to make or rotate a key
